### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **133** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 57 pages)`
- **17** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b39ce2dfe9e1360153ceb34adbd9883e28d74bfe` — the merge of head `711e6d9603e40cedf726ab5f29ed991196a5daba` into base `e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b39ce2dfe9e1360153ceb34adbd9883e28d74bfe && git checkout b39ce2dfe9e1360153ceb34adbd9883e28d74bfe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9 711e6d9603e40cedf726ab5f29ed991196a5daba && git checkout -B drift-repro e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9 && git merge --no-ff 711e6d9603e40cedf726ab5f29ed991196a5daba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e6a0b72a90ec4124aa908cfd05e9cb04a1a0b1b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `711e6d9603e40cedf726ab5f29ed991196a5daba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/declared-rename.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-declared-rename.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-declared-renames.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/spec/liveness/field.json

The rest of the diff (the four test files, the dogfood pin, `schema-drift.ts`, `index.ts`, `sql-driver-facet-hosts.ts`, `schema-migrate.ts`, `check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs`, the six changesets, the liveness README and counts shard, `content/docs/**`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; code there was read to judge the files above, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Spec accept set: unchanged — right.** `field.zod.ts` changes the `renamedFrom` docblock and `.describe()` only; the array-of-snake-case shape and `refuseDishonestRenamedFrom` are untouched. The three generated reference pages (`references/data/field`, `data/object`, `system/migration`) carry the new describe text byte for byte; no file on the head still carries "until that step ships" outside the changeset that quotes it. `packages/spec/json-schema/` does not emit field descriptions, so nothing there is stale.
- **Liveness ledger: `renamedFrom` `planned` → `live` — right.** `field.json` cites `sql-driver-declared-rename.ts#carryDeclaredRenames`, `declared-rename.ts#planDeclaredRenames` and `marketplace-install-declared-renames.ts#planInstallDeclaredRenames` with `verifiedAt` 2026-11-08; the counts shard moves planned 6 → 5, live 105 → 106 and the README note says the same. `Spec property liveness` is green on this head.
- **driver-sql public surface widens — right, minor.** Five new `SqlDriver` members (`declaredRenameLimit`, `planDeclaredRenames`, `carryDeclaredRenames`, `reverseDeclaredRenames`, `retireIndexesNamedForOldKeys`), three value exports plus four type exports from `index.ts`, `PendingSchemaWorkKind` gains `rename_columns`, `PendingSchemaWork` gains optional `renames`. Nothing removed.
- **cloud-connection door: `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` removed, `422` / `503` / `500` added, success answer gains `renamesCarried` (omitted when empty) — right.** The 501 was #30884's interim answer and the card's Expected 4 orders its removal; `renamesCarried` is not in any published spec schema (no `overrideCollisions` / `translationsLoaded` / `renamesCarried` under `packages/spec/src`), so it is not a Clause-② surface.
- **driver-turso REMOTE face: five overrides, five `REMOTE_FACE_ANSWERS` rows — right.** `syncSchema`, `initObjects` and `syncSchemasBatch` ask `refuseRemoteDeclaredRenames` before the transport's additive sync, so a pending carry throws `transport` instead of adding an empty column; reverse and retire answer 501 by name.
- **cli: `rename_columns` rendered and counted, excluded from the in-place total — right.**
- **Skills: one table row and one eval added, three restatements deleted for the token ratchet — right.** The deleted clauses ("(additive)", "Relaxing `required` alone changes no column", "a conditional contract cannot be an unconditional column constraint") are each still taught by the paragraph that follows the table.
- **Check-runs on the head (read at 07:14Z, the head pushed ~07:08Z).** Completed success: Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Auto Label, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Check Documentation Links, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, filter, Flag docs affected by code changes, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness. **Still in progress, not waited for:** Build Core, Test Core (1–8/8), Test UI (1–16/16), Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · repo & tooling gates. Skipped: Lint UI, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood matrix shards, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), the three opt-in gates. ⚠ The MySQL live cell is therefore unmeasured on this head (a named skip locally, and the only CI job that runs it skipped on this PR); the card's acceptance names SQLite and Postgres only, so this is a note, not a finding.

### ② Semver level

Six changesets, one per package the diff moves: `@objectstack/driver-sql` minor, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` minor, `@objectstack/driver-turso` minor, `@objectstack/cli` minor, `@objectstack/skills` minor (a real package, `packages/skills/package.json`), `@objectstack/spec` minor (`30885-spec-renamed-from-live`). Each carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, matching the PR body's two lines.

- **`30885-spec-renamed-from-live` — matches the tree.** Its body says the ledger row flips, the describe and docblock now say what the sync does "in place of 'until that step ships, no upgrade carries a column'", the generated pages follow, and "No schema shape changes" — every clause is true of the diff. `semantic` is the right kind: the key's declared meaning moves from inert-by-declaration to carried, with no key added or refused; AGENTS.md § 3 makes a kind take at least `minor` on a moved package, so `minor` follows. `Clause-②: no` holds: the published accept set of `FieldSchema` is byte-identical, the install-local answer is not a published schema, and nothing narrows.
- The other five are `minor` for genuine surface additions (new exports, members, kinds, HTTP answers) and are the lane seat's.
- `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the dev report — none to answer.
- The report's ten `deviations` are each visible in the diff and each is answered: the two new driver-sql modules and the facet stubs are the "sync/apply sites" the order named; the door's planner module keeps the 6.7k-line plugin file whole; the turso table pins every member so the five had to be classified; the cli print, the dogfood pin, the skills row, the cli.mdx sentence, the ledger README/counts, and the tenant-chokepoint hint are each the gate's or the ledger's own prescription. "`objectql/package-upgrade-environment.ts` and the registry merge untouched" is true on the head, and scope addition 1 (extension fields) is answered at the door (`outside_package`, `live_key`) rather than in the registry fold — an acceptable placement, since only the door knows which package installs.
- The report's `out_of_scope_findings` item 1 (the `.describe()` still saying "until that step ships") has since been taken up **inside this PR**: commit `71c22bf9` rewrote the docblock and describe, so the item is closed on the head. See nit N3 for the PR-body paragraph this left stale.
- Scope addition 2 (builtin and tenant columns) is answered by `platform_column` (`BUILTIN_COLUMNS`, the table's tenant column, a `__hash` shadow). Scope addition 3 (the one docs sentence) is in `data-modeling/fields.mdx` and in the eval's expected output.
- No flag is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (hits) — against `carryDeclaredRenames`, `planDeclaredRenames` and the install door, sentence by sentence.**

- "Read only by the schema sync and the install-local door; no record read, write or query reads it." Readers on the head: `declared-rename.ts#renamedFromOf` (sync and preview), `marketplace-install-declared-renames.ts#renamedFromOf` (door), `metadata-core/package-upgrade-plan.ts#comparePackageVersions` (the plan the door runs), and the two parse-time doors. `object-schema-fls-references.ts` only passes the key through a projection (`keep`). No CRUD or query path reads it. **Holds.**
- "The SQL driver's sync renames the old column to this key (`carryDeclaredRenames`, before the additive `ADD COLUMN`)." `RotationFacet.initObjects` existing-table branch: `await this.carryDeclaredRenames(tableName, obj)` precedes `columnInfo()` and the `alterTable` that adds columns. **Holds.**
- "so every path that syncs a schema carries it: a boot on the new artifact, `os migrate apply`, and `/marketplace/install-local`". `SchemaSyncSectionFacet.syncSchema` → `initObjects` (boot and `ObjectQL.syncSchemas`); `DeferredDdlFacet.flushDeferredSchemaDdl` → `initObjects` (`os migrate apply`); the door carries at step 2f and its post-register `syncSchemas()` finds nothing left to plan. **Holds.**
- "which carries before it registers the new version and puts the column back if that fails." Step 2f precedes step 3 (`register`); the register `catch` calls `reverseInstallDeclaredRenames(carried, …)` on every branch; a carry that throws mid-way reverses the tables already carried (`carryInstallDeclaredRenames`). **Holds.**
- "A rename it cannot carry is refused before any write, naming the field, the old key and the reason." `planDeclaredRenames` is pure; the facet reads `columnInfo`, `introspectColumns`, `introspectIndexes` and writes nothing; `carryDeclaredRenames` throws `DeclaredRenameRefusal` before `executeDeclaredRenames`; each entry carries `field`, `from`, `reason`, `message`. **Holds — with the one exception in S1 below.**
- Describe: "the type of the old column is judged when the column is carried, not here." The facet runs `diffManagedTable` over the old column read under the new declaration. **Holds.**
- Describe: refuses "when the old key is a platform column or still a live field, when both columns or several old columns exist, when the old column would narrow under this type, when an index cannot follow, or when the driver renames no column." Maps one to one onto `platform_column`, `live_key`, `both_columns`, `several_old_columns`, `destructive_type`, `index_cannot_follow`, `transport`. "Would narrow" is exact: on the head the only `destructive` op in `TYPE_DRIFT_OPS` is `narrow_varchar` (`manual_column_type_change` is emitted `needs_confirm` only, `widen_varchar` `safe`, `manual_widen_varchar_to_text` `needs_confirm`). `claimed_twice` is unnamed in the describe but is the runtime twin of the parse-time refusal the same sentence already states. **Holds.**
- Idempotency: after a carry the table has `b` and no `a`; `present` is empty and the planner `continue`s; a second sync, `os migrate plan`, and the door's post-register sync each plan nothing. **Holds.**
- Atomicity: PG/SQLite inside `knex.transaction`; MySQL every rename of one table in ONE `ALTER TABLE … RENAME COLUMN …, RENAME COLUMN …`. **Holds.**
- Indexes follow: all three dialects carry indexes with a `RENAME COLUMN`; `retireIndexesNamedForOldKeys` drops the old-named index only once `syncTableIndexes` has created the one named for the new key over the same key, and only names `buildIndexName` produces. The MySQL hash-shadow carrier, which cannot follow, is refused by name. **Holds.**

**S1 — should-fix — a virtual rename target is silently inert on the sync paths while the door refuses it.** `declared-rename.ts:143`: `if (BUILTIN_COLUMNS.has(field) || !fieldHasColumn(def)) continue;`. A field `b: formula … renamedFrom: ['a']` parses (neither parse-time door looks at the type), and on a boot, `os start`/`os dev` or `os migrate apply` over a table that still holds column `a` the planner skips it: no carry, no refusal, no log line, `os migrate plan` lists nothing, and the old column is left as an orphan for the drift pass to report later under another name. The install door judges the same declaration `destructive_type` (`typeChangeCategory` stored → virtual is `destructive`, and `planInstallDeclaredRenames` refuses it 422). So the three paths the card insists carry alike disagree on one declaration, and the describe's promise — "refuses before any write, naming the field, the old key and the reason" for what it cannot carry — has one case that is neither carried nor named, the "silently inert" shape the ledger note (ADR-0078) rules out. Fix in the planner: when `!fieldHasColumn(def)` and some `usable` old key is in `physicalColumns`, push a `destructive_type` refusal ("this type stores no column, so the values in 'a' have nowhere to go") instead of `continue`; a formula target with no old column left stays a no-op. Alternatively refuse `renamedFrom` on a virtual type at parse in `field.zod.ts`. Either fix moves the head and owes a delta review. No data is lost or miscarried on the head, hence not must-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (hits) — against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches.** The new row "rename a field → `renamedFrom: ['old_key']` on the new key: the sync carries the column's values" sits under "Existing DB on restart", where it is exactly what `initObjects` now does, and it replaces "rename" in the `os migrate apply` row, which never had a rename op. The row agrees with the describe on the head and with `data-modeling/fields.mdx`. The three deletions change no teaching (judged in ①). **Holds.**

**`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` (hits).** Eval 10's prompt is the card's scenario (a package's `lead.company` with production data, renamed to `account_name` in the next version). The expected output — key `account_name`, `renamedFrom: ['company']`, remove `company`, the sync renames the column values and all, keep the entry while any installed version may still carry the old key — matches the describe and scope addition 3; the assertions (`renamedFrom`, `account_name`) are the minimum a right answer must contain. **Holds, with nit N2.**

**N2 — nit (prose face) — eval 10's "without" sentence conflates the two paths.** "Without `renamedFrom` the new key is a new, empty column and the upgrade stops on a suspected rename": on the install door the 409 stops the upgrade before any column exists; on a restart the additive sync adds the empty column and nothing stops. For a package-upgrade prompt the second half is the one that happens. "Without `renamedFrom` a package upgrade is refused on a suspected rename, and a plain restart would add `account_name` as an empty column beside `company`" says both truly. No effect on the assertions or the contract.

**N3 — nit (PR body, not the tree) — the "Owed to the spec lane (not changed here)" paragraph is stale.** It says the `renamedFrom` `.describe()` and the three generated pages still end "until that step ships…" and are left for the spec seat; commit `71c22bf9` on this head rewrote them inside this PR, and the `30885-spec-renamed-from-live` changeset says so. The body's file-level "Deviations" list also omits `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` and `content/docs/references/**`. A PR-body edit; the head does not move.

**Implementing files — tried to break, held.** `both_columns` is judged on the old keys actually present, so a half-done table is refused, never guessed. `live_key` and `claimed_twice` run on the merged map at boot (an extension's field counts) and on the "map the upgrade leaves" at the door (`liveKeys`), so an owner's just-dropped key cannot be taken by another package's extension (`outside_package`). The door plans at 2c″ before the 409 of 2c′, writes nothing until 2f, and `installedRecordUnavailableVerdict` no longer answers 501 — the token now admits an unchecked re-install while a pending rename it cannot carry is still refused by `transport` / `outside_package`. `findConflict` is `'none' | 'marketplace' | 'user-code'` only, so `installed = null` is a genuine fresh install. `previewDeferredSchemaWork` mirrors the sync (a refusal is `refuse_table` with the same renderer; a carry is subtracted from `missing`). The Turso REMOTE plan reuses the pure planner on `pragma_table_info` and keeps the planner's own refusals beside the `transport` ones. `retireIndexesNamedForOldKeys` runs only under `exists` and only after `syncTableIndexes`, so the new-named index stands before the old is dropped. `assertSchemaMutable` is asked on carry and reverse and skipped for objects declaring none, so a production boot with auto-DDL off behaves as the rest of the sync does.
